lawyer:
Sagir Hossain, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners. 
Sikder Mahmudur Rani, Advocate ----- For the Respondent No. 3.
parties:
Atiqullah (Md) and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Artha Rin Adalat and others ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Anwarul Haque J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh this Rule was issued calling upon the respondent Nos. 2- 3 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 15-9-2008 passed by the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2 Dhaka in Artha Execution Case No. 116 of 2007 issuing a certificate in favour of a decree-holder under sub-section 7 of section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The petitioner took loan of Taka 3,10,00,000 (three crore and ten lakh) from respondent No. 3 AI-Arafah Islam Bank Limited, Maulavi Bazar Branch at Dhaka who ultimately become defaulter to the tune of Taka 5,36,25,101.75 as on 19-4-2005 for which Artha Rin Suit No. 74 of 2005 was filed and on transfer it was re-numbered as 7 of 2006 where the present petitioners made their appearance and filed written statement in order to contest the suit. On final hearing the suit was decreed on contest against the defendant Nos. 1-4, 5-9' and ex-parte against the rest directing the defendant-petitioner to pay the decretal amount to the tune of Taka 5,36,25,101.75 as on 19-4-2005 with a further direction to pay interest in terms of the provisions laid down in sub-section (2) of section 50 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 within 60 days. Against such direction, the Writ Petition No. 4257 of 2003 was filed by the present petitioner but such writ petition was discharged for non-prosecution. Thereafter, for execution of such decree the decree-holder filed this Execution Case No. 116 of 2007. 

 4. During the course of disposal of the execution case judgment-debtor, the petitioners, also made their appearance on receipt of the notice under section 30 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Thereafter, on 12-7-2007, the judgment-debtors, filed an application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 with a prayer to stay the sale of the mortgaged property on the ground of pendency of the Writ Petition No. 4257 of 2003. Considering such prayer the Court become slow to proceed with the execution case and re-called the order passed under section 33(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Thereafter, on 11-3-2008 such Writ Petition No. 4257 of 2003 is found to have been discharged for non-prosecution allowing the decree-holder to proceed with the execution case. To dispose of the execution case again the notice under section 33(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was issued and parties were asked to published a notice in "Dainik Prothom Alo" and "Dainik Sangbad" but none I found to participate in the auction bid. On failure to sell the property in auction in order to realize the decretal amount along with interest, the respondent being decree-holder filed an application with a prayer to transfer the title of the mortgage property in his favour under the provision laid down in section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and accordingly obtained such certificate on 15-9-2008. Then, the judgment-debtor, the present petitioner has again jumped upon this writ jurisdiction and obtained the present Rule and order of stay on 23-10-2008. 

 5. Mr. Md. Sagir Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that without compliance of the provision laid down in sub-section (4) & (5) of section 33, the decree-holder has preserved no right to obtain certificate under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which, in fact, amounts to a title deed, to be registered by the concerned Sub-Registrar without any cost. He goes to argue that the mortgage property has got a higher value than that of decretal amount; as such the ownership of the property by way of certificate under the provision of section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 will cause irreparable loss to the petitioner and there will be no scope to comply with the provision of sub-section (6) of section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The learned Advocate for the petitioner-judgment debtor has also argued that had there been any opportunity to sell the property in auction certainly the value of the property would be more than 20 crones where the petitioner is entitled to get back the balance amount there: as such the very issuance of certificate, under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is to be declared illegal and without any lawful authority and has got no legal effect. 

 6. On the other hand, Mr. Sikder Mahmudur Razi, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the Respondent No. 3, has opposed. the Rule alleging inter also that on failure to sell the mortgaged property for the purpose of realization of the decretal amount under section 33(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the decree-holder has restored under the provision of under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 where no pre-condition of publishing the auction notice under section 33(4) has been imposed because the provision of sub-section (7) of section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is independent one. Moreover, the publication of auction notice in "Dainik Prothom Alo" and "Dainik Sangbad" has fulfilled the requirement of sub-section (7) of section 33 because none has turned up to purchase the property in auction. Moreover, regarding of such publication in the form of proclamation as argued by the learned Advocate for the petitioner cannot be accepted because the provision of law employed in sub-section (1) of section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 does not demand so. Moreover, the order 12-8-2008 and 15-9-2008 (Annexure-G to the petition) also stands to say that the proclamations have been duly returned with service; as such the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner deserves no consideration and accordingly, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 8. In order to have a resort under sub-section (7) of section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the judgment-debtor is not required to follow the provision of sub-section (4) & (5) rather to follow the provision of sub-section (1), (2) and (3) of section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Moreover, the application is found to have failed by the decree-holder before issuance of such certificate. 

 9. It appears from the order sheet (Annexure-G to the petition ) of the execution case that Court has followed the provision of sub-section (1) of section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in order to put the mortgage-property in auction but failed; as such when the decree-holder filed an application as required under sub-section (7) of section 33 of the said Ain the Court is at liberty to issue certificate when application has been filed by the decree-holder. So, there is no illegality or infirmity in the order of issuance of the certificate dated 15-9-2008, which is awaiting for registration under sub-section (8) of section 33 of the said Ain. In fact, on perusal of the application and the conduct of the petitioner we are convinced that he is in the habit of filing one after another writ petition in different angle in order to drag the execution case in his own manner in order to delay in realising the decretal amount which should not be allowed to continue more. This type of conduct of the petitioners is to be condemned by imposing cost of Taka 50,000 (fifty thousands).
